texts.preamble: Pawanshree Food International Private ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 August, 2025
texts.facts: By this petition preferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India the petitioner has challenged the notice dated 27.06.2025 (Annexure P/1) issued by the Additional District Magistrate, District Indore whereby he has been directed to submit his reply through the authorized officer of the company. 2. On 11.09.2024 respondent No.1 raided a firm in the name of Satyam Traders, Indore and found that the Food Business Operator had various edible items stored for human consumption. Samples of Shreedhi Ghee Agmark Special Grade 15 Kg. and Shreedhi Ghee (made from cow milk) Agmark Special Grade 15 Kg. were taken and sent for analysis. In the analysis the samples were found to be substandard and of inferior quality. Various other irregularities were also found. 3. Thereafter application under Section 68 of the Food and Safety NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:23956 2 WP-32494-2025 Standard Act was filed against the manufacturers of the spurious ghee. During investigation notice was given to respondents 2 and 3 to establish the source of procuring the product. Respondents 2 and 3 stated that they do not have any bill pertaining to purchase of the ghee from the petitioner. During the course of proceedings the impugned notice has been issued to the petitioner. Pawanshree Food International Private ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104873811/ 1 4. Impleadment of the petitioner is hence illegal.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that since respondents 2 and 3 have admitted that they do not have any bill of purchase of the ghee from the petitioner he could not have been impleaded as a party to the proceedings. As per the investigation no invoice/cash memo was presented during investigation nor after its completion respondents 2 and 3 have stated that they procured the ghee from the petitioner.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that since respondents 2 and 3 have admitted that they do not have any bill of purchase of the ghee from the petitioner he could not have been impleaded as a party to the proceedings. As per the investigation no invoice/cash memo was presented during investigation nor after its completion respondents 2 and 3 have stated that they procured the ghee from the petitioner.
